thread:
Sam P: Heads-up — rolled a Canary that prefers INT8 KV kernels for >1k cached tokens. Observing weird tail latency spikes on short-decoder workloads (most requests ~16-32 tokens).
Kira: saw that on staging. p50 up ~6-8% for short requests. Do you have the profiling traces?
Sam P: grabbed a few. Short sample: baseline FP8-KV (old): p50=42ms, p95=118ms, KV mem=2.1GB. INT8-KV (new): p50=45ms, p95=160ms, KV mem=1.05GB. So mem cut ~50% but p95 regressed a lot.
Ravi: that p95 jump smells like kernel switch thrash or extra synchronization. Any per-request kernel switch logs?
Kira: yes. Profiling shows frequent kernel selection decisions inside the decode loop when batch size/buffer length oscillates. Each decision path triggers a cuda event + small memcpy when switching the KV layout. Stack snippet:
```
if (seq_len > 512 && kv_quant==INT8) select_kernel(INT8_Packed);
else select_kernel(FP8_Packed);
// -> call kernel; kv_layout conversion may occur inline
```
Marta: inline conversion? that's the killer. We convert KV layout on the hot path for compatibility. That adds ~0.8ms per invocation but it's called many times for beam/streaming cases.
Sam P: exact numbers from perf-bot trace:
- kernel_select: 0.6ms/call
- kv_layout_convert (memcpy+pack): 0.9ms/call
- kernel_launch_ht: 0.2ms/call
- decode_step_total: baseline 3.2ms -> experiment 3.9ms (short seq)
perf-bot: attached flamegraph id=flame-193000-A1 (uploaded to perf dashboard)
Kira: Another interesting bit — batching heuristic resets on small gaps in arrival times. When a batch shrinks below threshold we fall back to a different execution path which triggers layout conversion. So jitter in arrival patterns amplifies the cost.
Ravi: So two levers: 1) avoid inline KV conversion (do conversion lazily or during cache fill), 2) make kernel selection stable across short-term batch fluctuations. Also consider keeping an INT8-compatible layout for both kernels and avoid conversion entirely at cost of a bit more memory.
Marta: For the decode-quality side — we ran the calibration for INT8 using per-head symmetric quant with layerwise scales. Observed slight decode drift on long-tail tokens: avg token logprob delta ~ -0.02, EM on our QA suite down 0.6% (stat sig). FP8 baseline has near-zero drift.
Sam P: can you paste the calibration command and flags used?
Kira: sure:
```
./calibrate_kv --model=/mnt/models/7b --dataset=calib_small.json --method=per_head_sym --clip=3.0 --reduce=mean
```
Ravi: per_head_sym + clip=3.0 might be too aggressive on some heads. Also we saw a few heads with heavy tails; symmetric quantization introduces bias on those. Suggest testing per-channel/asymmetric for KV-only.
Marta: ran a quick A/B: INT8-perchannel (same mem) improved EM drop to 0.2% and reduced avg logprob delta to -0.008. Nice. Throughput slightly worse vs per_head (p50 ~ +1ms) but p95 improved because we removed layout conversions.
Sam P: summary: INT8 gives ~50% KV mem savings; but naive kernel switching + inline conversion causes p95 regressions. Calibration choice affects quality; per-channel helps.
Kira: proposed next steps:
- Stop doing layout conversion inline during decode. Move conversion to a background task when populating cache pages (async). (Small PR)
- Add hysteresis to kernel selection: require sustained sequence-length/batch-size window before switching kernels. (Medium PR)
- Experiment with a unified KV layout that both INT8 and FP8 kernels can consume (fast path). (Spike)
- Add a calibration suite to validate quantization configs against a small eval set and emit warning if EM/logprob delta > threshold. (Tooling)
Ravi: I can take the hysteresis change. Suggest interface: kernel_policy.keep_current_for=200ms or N decode steps; plus sample-based detection: if >70% of last 50 steps lean INT8, then switch.
Marta: I'll work async on per-channel calibration comparison and push bench results to the dashboard. Will include sample perplexity, avg token logprob, and QA EM.
Sam P: small perf note: when we moved layout convert out-of-band on a tiny experiment, p95 dropped from 160ms -> 125ms, p50 stayed ~45ms. So it's promising.
Kira: also noticed CUDA memcopy path was using pageable fallback occasionally on our nodes which added 0.5ms jitter. Ensure we use pinned buffers for conversions.
perf-bot: schedule: nightly/regression check added -> test-suite "kv-quant-smoke" triggers after canary deploys.
Ravi: Should we roll back canary until hysteresis patch lands?
Sam P: let's pause the canary for public endpoints. Keep it active on staging and dedicated clusters for more data.
Marta: copying notes to the perf runbook and opening a small ticket for pinned-buffer fallback.
Kira: TL;DR: INT8 KV = big memory wins, but watch out for kernel thrash + inline conversions + calibration choices. Short-term: move conversion off hot path + hysteresis. Medium: explore unified layout.
Sam P: thanks team, will file the canary pause + link PRs. :thumbsup!
